```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", fig.align = "center")
```

```{r}
library(tidymarkers)
library(knitr)
```

Every figure shows sequence letters (spacer/PAM, primers and amplicon), the
variant track, the genomic off-site panel and, on the right, the same tumbler as
for KASP.
Two schemes at opposite ends of the spectrum: CRISPR-Dx gives a
binary/fluorescent signal through collateral cleavage, Sanger reads the base
directly. Both require a unique target and a careful oligo geometry.

## CRISPR-Dx: Cas12a and Cas13

Cas12a is guided by a spacer of ~20 nt and requires a PAM (for Cas12a usually
TTTV) next to the protospacer. On a match, collateral ssDNase activity is
activated, which cuts the ssDNA reporter – the signal is amplified. Cas13 works
on an RNA target; no PAM is needed, but there is a PFS (Cas13a – avoid G at the
3′ flank, Cas13b – 5′ D-PFS); the spacer sets specificity.
[Chen et al. (2018)](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aar6245),
[Gootenberg et al. (2017)](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aam9321).

The package checks PAM/spacer, GC, the absence of exact off-target protospacers
and the preamplification (RPA). Collateral kinetics is not simulated – this is
recorded in `marker_readout()`.

```{r crispr-fig, echo = FALSE, out.width = "100%", fig.cap = "CRISPR-Dx: spacer, PAM and preamplicon; cleavage kinetics is not modelled."}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/crispr.svg")
```

```{r, eval = FALSE}
snp <- tibble::tibble(chrom = "Chr1", pos = 300L, ref = "T", alt = "A")
design_crispr_marker(genome, snp, flank = 200, cas = "cas12a")
```

## Sanger

Sanger sequencing reads the variant directly: a flanking pair gives a 400–800 bp
amplicon, and nested read primers read through the variant from both sides.
There is no "primer-based" discrimination – there is read quality.
[Sanger et al. (1977)](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.74.12.5463).

The key point: the variant must be far enough from the read ends (usually
>= 50 bp), the amplicon unique, and the read primers inside the product, not
conflicting with the amplification ones.

```{r sanger-fig, echo = FALSE, out.width = "100%", fig.cap = "Sanger: flanking amplicon and nested read primers."}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/sanger.svg")
```

```{r, eval = FALSE}
design_sanger_marker(genome, snp, flank = 500)
```

## Failed markers and missing checks

A design may pass every gate and still give an "empty" marker (a dud marker): no
signal, no discrimination, or a signal that comes from the wrong target. Some of
these cases are visible at once – `design_crispr_marker()`/`design_sanger_marker()`
return `NULL`; some pass design and fail only in the lab. Below are specific
cases. **In the package** – the check is actually computed or gated;
**recommendation** – this is not in the model, check it by hand.

### CRISPR-Dx

- **PAM/spacer conservation in the population.** **In the package:** the search
  runs on one reference sequence; `design_crispr_marker()` does not look into
  VCF/population data. A frequent SNP in the spacer, seed or PAM will break
  binding in part of the genotypes. **Recommendation:** check population variation
  in the spacer/PAM/seed; PAM and seed – [Addgene CRISPR Guide](https://www.addgene.org/guides/crispr/),
  seed mismatches – [Kleinstiver et al. (2016)](https://doi.org/10.1038/nbt.3620).

- **PAM/PFS for a specific Cas variant.** **In the package:** `cas12a` (5'-TTTV),
  `cas13`/`cas13a` (3′ non-G PFS) and `cas13b` (5′ D-PFS); there is no separate
  model for other enzymes/PAMs (Cas12b/Cas12i/Cas12j, Cas9,
  Cas14, engineered Cas12a with an altered PAM). For an engineered Cas12a,
  `cas = "cas12a"` will apply TTTV even if the enzyme has a different PAM.
  **Recommendation:** take the PAM from the table for the real enzyme
  ([Addgene](https://www.addgene.org/guides/crispr/)); Cas13 cuts RNA, not DNA
  (the DNA target is first preamplified and transcribed through T7)
  ([Gootenberg et al. (2017)](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aam9321),
  [2018](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aaq0179)).

- Off-target cleavage.** **In the package:** `crispr_spacer_hits()` counts the
  exact occurrences of the spacer and its reverse complement,
  `off_target = hits - 1`; this is a hard gate (`specificity_max = 0`). It is not
  an off-target prediction: the PAM of the found copies is not checked, mismatches
  are not scored, and collateral cleavage at off-targets is not modelled.
  **Recommendation:** for complex/repetitive genomes, use a mismatch-aware search
  (seed/PAM) and validation; Cpf1 specificity –
  [Kleinstiver et al. (2016)](https://doi.org/10.1038/nbt.3620).

- **Preamplification (RPA).** **In the package:** the RPA pair flanks the spacer,
  the RPA length/GC windows and the amplicon of 80–250 bp are checked (a soft gate
  widened by 20 bp). Uniqueness of the pair across the genome is not a design
  gate; RPA kinetics and primer artefacts are not modelled; for Cas13 the T7
  orientation is not validated.
  **Recommendation:** run in-silico PCR/uniqueness for the preamplification pair
  and check the RPA ([Piepenburg et al. (2006)](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pbio.0040204)).

- **Target strand.** **In the package:** both strands are scanned by default,
  `strand = "+"`/`"-"` narrows the search; for Cas13 this is the caller's
  responsibility – the spacer must match the transcribed (T7) strand, and there
  is no automatic T7 check. **Recommendation:** for Cas13, set `strand`
  explicitly and verify against the T7 construct
  ([Gootenberg et al. (2018)](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aaq0179)).

- **Reporter/probe readout.** **In the package:** the reporter/probe is not
  designed; `marker_readout()` returns `simulated = FALSE` and the note
  "Cas collateral-cleavage kinetics not modelled". **Recommendation:**
  calibrate "yes/no" in the lab; the mechanics of collateral cleavage –
  [Chen et al. (2018)](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aar6245).

- **Spacer secondary structure.** **In the package:** the spacer is visible in
  the shared oligo checks (`plot(marker)`: hairpin, dimer, inverted repeat,
  homopolymer, SSR), but `design_crispr_marker()` does not reject on them – they
  are not a design gate. The structure of the full crRNA/scaffold is not
  modelled. **Recommendation:** check the spacer/crRNA structure with an external
  tool, especially for GC-rich spacers.

- **SNP under seed/PAM.** **In the package:** the target variant is placed in the
  seed (Cas12a, offset < 8 nt) or in the central half of the spacer (Cas13, the
  package's approximation), and the guide is chosen for one allele. A second SNP
  under seed/PAM is not taken into account. If the variant falls in the PAM, it
  is not in the spacer of that guide; if no alternative geometry exists, design
  returns `NULL`. **Recommendation:** check haplotypes in seed/PAM and change the
  strand/enzyme rather than "stretch" the guide.

### Sanger

- **Variant too close to the read start.** **In the package:** the hard
  `gate_sanger_dist` requires >= 50 bp from the variant to each read start;
  otherwise `design_sanger_marker()` returns `NULL`. The first
  ~50 bases of a read are traditionally of low quality
  ([molbiologytools](https://molbiologytools.com/sanger_primer_designer_help);
  [Sanger et al. (1977)](https://doi.org/10.1073/pnas.74.12.5463)).

- **Poor read quality.** **In the package:** quality is not modelled; 50 bp is a
  fixed heuristic, not Phred. Homopolymers/SSRs are checked for the primers, not
  for the amplicon; a GC-rich stretch may "collapse" beyond 50 bp as well.
  **Recommendation:** look at the real chromatogram and trim the low-quality
  ends.

- **Heterozygous indel/phase.** **In the package:** a single `snp` (`ref`/`alt`),
  without homo/heterozygosity and phasing; mixed peaks are not modelled.
  **Recommendation:** for indels and phase, use cloning, allele-specific PCR or
  another scheme; Sanger reads the base directly, but by itself does not give
  phase.

- **Failure of the nested read primer.** **In the package:** read primers are
  searched in a window up to 40 bp from the PCR primers, with a Tm/GC screen and a
  preference for a low 3' homopolymer (not a hard filter); on failure it falls
  back to the flanking pair (`nested = FALSE`). 3'-seed uniqueness is checked only
  for an in-memory `DNAStringSet`; for an indexed `marker_genome` the check is
  skipped (`NA`). **Recommendation:** order both variants; overlap/competition of
  the read and PCR primers is not modelled.

- **PCR product contamination.** **In the package:** `gate_sanger_unique` is
  genomic specificity (one in-silico product, no exact off-target hits), not assay
  purity. Contamination/carryover is not modelled. **Recommendation:** NTC/negative
  controls, fresh reagents, a gel; contamination gives a "heterozygous" picture
  that is easily taken for real.

- **Variant outside the quality window of the read.** **In the package:** the
  gate holds only the lower bound (>= 50 bp) and prefers a central position (the
  "variant centrality" tier), but does not check the read length/upper bound. A
  variant in the far half of an 800-bp amplicon may not fall in the read.
  **Recommendation:** compare the expected read length with the variant position;
  read with the reverse primer or shorten the amplicon.

- **No chromatogram simulation.** **In the package:** `marker_readout()` for
  Sanger returns `simulated = FALSE` and the note "read / peak model not simulated";
  `design_sanger_marker()` returns the amplicon and primers, not a trace.
  **Recommendation:** interpret only a real chromatogram, and treat the design as
  a geometric check.

These limitations do not make the design useless: they separate the geometry the
package has checked from the biology that has to be checked in the lab.

### Decision audit

`vignettes/figures/decision-crispr.txt` and `decision-sanger.txt` describe the
scheme, not a run trace: `marker_decision_text()` assembles the nodes from
`marker_criteria()` and `scheme_def_*()`. Below is a comparison of the template
with what `design_crispr_marker()` / `design_sanger_marker()` actually execute,
and with the panels in `vignettes/figures/crispr.svg` / `sanger.svg`. Labels:
**executed** – the node is really computed; **declarative** – it is in the
template but not in the code; **in the figure** – a `plot()` panel, not a gate.

```{r, echo = FALSE, out.width = "100%"}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/decision-crispr.svg")
```

```{r, echo = FALSE, out.width = "100%"}
knitr::include_graphics("figures/decision-sanger.svg")
```

**CRISPR-Dx: the graph is more declarative than the code.**
- **Declarative.** PAM, seed and specificity are drawn as hard, but on a
  returned marker they can hardly ever be `FALSE`: PAM is filtered by the scan
  (`TRUE` or `NA` for Cas13), seed is a scan condition (`TRUE`), specificity
  discards candidates before return. The edges `PAM → DOOMED` and
  `seed → DOOMED` are therefore diagnostic: the code returns a single `NULL` with
  a generic message, not a `marker_doomed` with a reason. The PAM node is not
  parameterised by enzyme (TTTV for Cas12a, `NA` for Cas13), and there is no
  separate strand node: `strand` is scanned, T7 orientation is not checked
  ([Gootenberg et al. (2017)](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aam9321);
  PAM/seed – [Addgene](https://www.addgene.org/guides/crispr/)). The `readout`
  line in the header is the only place where the reporter is mentioned; there is
  no kinetics/threshold node in the graph.
- **Declarative.** Tiers are not executed lexicographically. Graph: guide/PAM
  quality → variant position → off-target count → amplicon. The code sorts
  candidates by `v_off` (Cas12a) or centrality (Cas13), then by GC, and takes the
  first with a suitable RPA pair; `off-target count` with `specificity_max = 0`
  is always 0 (the tier is degenerate), and the amplicon length is not maximised.
- **Partially executed.** The RPA node is `design_flanking_pair()`
  (length/GC/product), not `design_rpa_marker()`: structure, probe and
  preamplification uniqueness are not gated. The ideogram in `crispr.svg` may
  show a second product, but the design does not reject it; RPA as a method –
  [Piepenburg et al. (2006)](https://doi.org/10.1371/journal.pbio.0040204).
- **In the figure.** The tumbler in `crispr.svg` is oligo QC, not gates: it
  computes `run`/`SSR`/`inv. repeat`/`hairpin`/`dimer`/`homodimer` for the guide
  and RPA primers, but `design_crispr_marker()` does not reject on these fields.
  `Tm guide` is deliberately `neutral` (no window), `off-target` is the exact
  hits of each oligo (max <= 1), not protospacers with a PAM.
- **Not modelled.** A single mismatch in the spacer is not scored: the guide is
  chosen for the reference, and the mismatch position (seed/distal) and type are
  not counted. A mismatch in the seed may preserve activity
  ([Kleinstiver et al. (2016)](https://doi.org/10.1038/nbt.3620)), and the
  collateral signal – [Chen et al. (2018)](https://doi.org/10.1126/science.aar6245).
  A refinement to "variant in PAM": by construction the variant always lies in
  the spacer, so the PAM of the returned guide does not contain it; the variant
  can only eliminate an alternative candidate.
- **Executed, but conservatively.** `crispr_spacer_hits()` subtracts 1 from the
  sum of exact hits in both orientations: a palindromic spacer may give a false
  `off_target`, hits without a PAM are counted, and mismatches are not searched
  at all. This is a conservative count, not an off-target prediction.

**Sanger: the graph is closer to the code.**
- **Executed.** `select_flanking_pair()` really applies the gate/relax/tier
  order, and `confirm()` adds `in_silico_pcr()` and `pair_structure_ok()`, so
  `decision-sanger.txt` is not just a declaration.
- **Executed, but the node is incomplete.** `gate_sanger_dist` (hard) is computed
  on the inner ends of the flanking pair (`end_f`/`start_r`); the nested read
  primers get their own `min_dist` later and have no separate node.
  `read F`/`read R` in the figure are primers, not read length; there is no upper
  read bound either in the graph or in the figure.
- **Executed conditionally; a refinement.** For `marker_genome` only the cheap
  3'-seed pre-screen is skipped (`m_unique = NA`); `gate_sanger_unique` is still
  closed by `in_silico_pcr()` in `confirm()`. Uniqueness is not "skipped". The
  figure has no in-silico product: `marker_ideogram()` looks for
  `forward`/`reverse`, while Sanger returns `PCR_F`/`PCR_R`.
- **Partially executed.** `pair_structure_ok()` does not check the cross-dimer
  and returns `TRUE` without OligoArrayAux; the tumbler in `sanger.svg` shows the
  cross-dimer, so the figure is stricter than the gate. Nested read primers are
  not structurally checked at all (only Tm/GC/3'-run/3'-seed).
- **Executed; a refinement.** The nested-primer fallback is per side: if only one
  is found, `nested = FALSE`, but the other side stays nested; this is not "the
  whole pair fell back to the flanking one".
- **Not modelled / absent from the figure.** The input is one `snp`; the figure
  draws one `T>A` track, so phase, mixed peaks and contamination cannot be proven
  from it. `marker_readout()` already marks Sanger as `simulated = FALSE`;
  `read F`/`read R` show primer placement, not a chromatogram.

## How to read these schemes

CRISPR-Dx answers "yes/no" (or semi-quantitatively by rate), Sanger answers
"which base exactly". Their gates therefore differ: for CRISPR, the hard
specificity of the spacer/PAM; for Sanger, the size and purity of the amplicon
plus the position of the read primers. What they share is target uniqueness and
the structure check of the oligos; `plot(marker)` shows the architecture,
`marker_readout()` what exactly is not modelled.
